summary: Cheap, rules-clean and shape-disjoint, with a safe fallback, so run it once with no companions. Expect at most a sub-microsecond gain at bs=1/8/16, because Marlin never triggers early and PDL here can only hide the dependent kernel's launch processing, not the tail of the w2 grid; judge it on the per-shape rows and the PATH CHOSEN line, not on the headline.
justification: Mechanism: launch_pdl plus gdc_wait (griddepcontrol.wait) on a Triton kernel captured into a CUDA graph becomes a programmatic edge, which is valid on H100 with CUDA 12.3+. In master's kernel_fn, the w2 moe_wna16_marlin_gemm is the node immediately before _post_norm_combine_kernel at num_tokens < 32: y.contiguous() is a no-op on the already contiguous view of cache3, and torch.empty for out launches nothing. So the edge exists. Size of the win: FINDINGS puts _post_norm_combine_kernel at 3.4/3.5/4.2 us at bs=1/8/16, against shape totals of 48.4/107.8/147.9 us (floors 11.4/37.3/52.5). Marlin is 87-93% of every shape, so the post-norm launch boundary is the only thing this touches. The hypothesis states the 1-2 us saving as fact, but it needs one of two things to be true: early triggering by the primary, or the inter-kernel gap in a graph replay being that large. WEAKEST LINK: 'overlap the tail of the w2 Marlin grid' is not what PDL does without a trigger. Marlin never calls griddepcontrol.launch_dependents, so its trigger is the implicit one at each block's exit. The dependent grid can be scheduled only after every Marlin block, last wave included, has exited. No post-norm block runs alongside the Marlin tail, and the pre-wait prologue (loading the 8 KB norm weight) hides almost nothing. What remains is the scheduling/launch latency between grid completion and the next node, typically about 0.3-1 us inside a graph. That is roughly 1-2% at bs=1, 0.5-1% at bs=8 and under 0.7% at bs=16, near or under per-shape noise. Headline: three of six loads gain at most about 1%, so the geomean moves about 0.3-0.5%, well inside the at-least-plus-or-minus-1.5% CI. A 'within-ci' headline is the most likely outcome and is uninformative by itself. The expected directions (faster at bs=1/8/16, flat at 32/128/256) agree with the code paths; only the magnitude is optimistic.
confounders: post-expert-norm-triton-small-m: this change only exists on top of it (it adds the Triton kernel that gets the PDL attribute). Reverting it removes the subject rather than isolating an interaction, so it does not confound. Note that its kernel's prologue is tiny, so the 'prologue overlap' part of the claim is at most a few hundred ns.

triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack / align-parallel-per-expert-verify / marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm: these change the align and the block_size_m pick. At bs<32 the restack's block_size_m pick decides how many w2 Marlin blocks run and how long the last wave is, which sets when the implicit trigger fires. That changes Marlin's own time, not the boundary saving, so it does not confound the A/B against master. The >=128 pieces are shape-disjoint.
sglang-marlin-path-parity: sets up the Marlin -> post-norm sequence itself. No interaction beyond being the base.

No landed hypothesis uses PDL. In-flight cuda-dispatch-combine-pdl-verify (PDL on the >32 combine) is shape-disjoint. post-norm-combine-hoisted-slot-loads and post-norm-triton-hoisted-decode32 edit the same kernel and must be restacked afterwards. cuda-fused-moe-bs1-persistent-w13-silu-w2 would remove the bs=1 boundary entirely if it lands.
interference: No companion is warranted. (i) ab-revert: there is no landed hypothesis whose removal would change how this result reads; the only one in the same area is this change's own substrate. (ii) ab-tune: the only knob that would change the mechanism is an early trigger in the primary (Marlin is a compiled sgl_kernel op that cannot be edited here) or a different pre-wait split. A 'gdc_wait at the very top' control would separate prologue overlap from launch-latency hiding, but both effects are sub-microsecond and a second run could not resolve the difference against noise. (iii) An A/A control of master to calibrate per-shape noise is impossible because identical code returns its cached result. Interpretation without companions: if the log says 'pdl off', the run measured master and says nothing about PDL. If 'pdl on', read the bs=1/8/16 per-shape paired ratios against master's rows (job 3cabc739f1af493e / BEST 45eacf4ca2e849d2) and treat bs=32/128/256 as the in-run control; if those drift as much as bs=1/8/16, the result is noise. A gain or loss inside the CI on the headline is expected and should not be read either way.
rules_flags: No rule break. PDL is an ordinary launch attribute, kernel_fn branches only on shape and state['pdl_ok'] (fixed in prepare), and there is no host sync and no input-derived caching.

The prepare() self-test must use only synthetic tensors it builds itself and must not keep the captured CUDAGraph or its buffers where kernel_fn could reuse them. Free them, or at least never touch them from kernel_fn. It runs untimed within the 300 s budget, which is fine.

Correctness hazard to keep closed: only post_norm_w loads (static weights) may come before gdc_wait. Every load of ids/tw/y and the store to out must stay after the wait. out is allocated from the graph pool after Marlin returns, so the allocator may reuse Marlin's internal temporaries (the fp32-reduce scratch) for it. A store before the wait could then race with Marlin. The hypothesis as written is correct; do not 'optimise' the store or the slot loads above the wait.

Compile/variant: launch_pdl is a Triton compile option, so it produces a different binary. Warming up both variants for every num_tokens < 32 in prepare (as specified) avoids compiling during the timed graph capture (that would be untimed anyway, but it costs against the 15-minute run limit).
open_questions: Do the judge's Triton (with torch 2.14.1) and CUDA driver have both the launch_pdl kwarg and tl.extra.cuda.gdc_wait, and does torch's stream capture turn the PDL attribute into a programmatic graph edge? The PATH CHOSEN line answers the first. The second is only observable as a timing delta, or as a self-test mismatch if the edge silently becomes a full dependency (correct but no gain).

Does moe_wna16_marlin_gemm launch anything after the Marlin kernel (for example a reduce or copy for use_fp32_reduce=True)? If it does, the PDL edge attaches to that tail kernel rather than to Marlin. That is still correct, but the 'w2 Marlin tail' framing does not apply. Confirm in the profile's kernel order at bs=1.

Is the inter-kernel gap at the Marlin -> post-norm boundary in the bs=1 graph replay actually 1-2 us? An nsys trace of master's bs=1 graph would settle whether the expected magnitude is reachable before spending a check.
